pharm: Humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody against CD6 on T cells that downregulates T-cell activation and proliferation and reduces proinflammatory cytokine production.

summary: Itolizumab is a humanized anti-CD6 IgG1 monoclonal antibody that modulates T-cell activity. By binding the CD6 receptor on T lymphocytes (which interacts with activated leukocyte cell adhesion molecule, ALCAM/CD166), it downregulates T-cell activation, proliferation, and the production of proinflammatory cytokines such as IFN-gamma, TNF-alpha, and IL-6, without broadly depleting T cells. It is used for chronic moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and, in some regions under emergency or restricted authorization, for cytokine release syndrome in severe COVID-19. A representative psoriasis regimen is 1.6 mg/kg by intravenous infusion every 2 weeks for 12 weeks, then every 4 weeks. Infusion reactions and infections are key safety concerns. NOTE: itolizumab is NOT approved by the US FDA; this record is based on Indian/regional regulatory and EMA-type sources.
indications: Chronic moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults (regional approval, e.g., India)
Cytokine release syndrome / acute respiratory distress in severe COVID-19 (restricted/emergency authorization in some regions)

moa: Itolizumab is a humanized recombinant IgG1 monoclonal antibody directed against CD6, a co-stimulatory receptor expressed predominantly on T lymphocytes. CD6 interacts with activated leukocyte cell adhesion molecule (ALCAM/CD166) and participates in T-cell activation, maturation, and trafficking. By binding the membrane-proximal domain of CD6, itolizumab downregulates T-cell activation and proliferation and reduces the production and release of proinflammatory cytokines (such as interferon-gamma, TNF-alpha, IL-6, and IL-17) without causing broad T-cell depletion, dampening the T-cell-driven inflammation underlying psoriasis and certain hyperinflammatory states.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to itolizumab or any excipient
Active severe infection (including active tuberculosis) until controlled
relative: History of chronic or recurrent infection or latent tuberculosis
Concurrent use of other immunosuppressants or live vaccines
monitor: Complete blood count (lymphocyte and white cell counts)
Tuberculosis status before and during therapy

preg: There are insufficient data on itolizumab use in pregnancy. As a monoclonal IgG antibody, it can cross the placenta, particularly in later pregnancy. Use should be avoided in pregnancy unless the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk; effective contraception is advised during treatment.
lact: It is not known whether itolizumab is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects in the breastfed infant and limited data, breastfeeding is generally not recommended during treatment.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment has been established for renal impairment; as a monoclonal antibody, itolizumab is not eliminated renally. Use with monitoring.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment has been established for hepatic impairment. Use with monitoring.

major: Other immunosuppressants/biologics - additive immunosuppression and infection risk
moderate: Other agents causing cytopenias - additive hematologic toxicity
minor: No significant small-molecule pharmacokinetic interactions established
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction documented; general moderation advised.
interactions.diagnostics: Screen for tuberculosis and assess complete blood count before and during therapy; live-vaccine response may be blunted.

pearls: NOT FDA-approved - this record is based on Indian/regional regulatory (CDSCO) and EMA-type sources; itolizumab is marketed in India (e.g., for plaque psoriasis) and used under restricted authorization for COVID-19 cytokine release syndrome in some regions
Anti-CD6 antibody modulates T-cell activation and proinflammatory cytokines WITHOUT broadly depleting T cells
Infusion-related reactions are common - premedicate and infuse slowly with monitoring
Screen for and avoid use in active infection/tuberculosis; avoid live vaccines
Monitor lymphocyte counts and for signs of immunosuppression-related infection
missed: Itolizumab is administered in a clinical setting on a scheduled basis. If an infusion appointment is missed, contact the treating physician or infusion center to reschedule as soon as possible; the dosing interval may be adjusted to maintain the treatment schedule.
overdose: There is limited information on itolizumab overdose. No specific antidote exists. In the event of overdose, monitor the patient closely for adverse reactions, particularly infusion reactions, immunosuppression, and infection, and provide supportive symptomatic treatment.
